section_summary: This section documents United States policy debates and administrative actions regarding the economic rehabilitation and deconcentration of postwar Japan between November 1947 and May 1948. It includes exchanges between the State and Army Departments over Far Eastern Commission debates on industrial credits, draft congressional legislation for occupied areas aid, and SCAP's implementation of the Deconcentration Law. Additional materials address the economic burden of American military dependents in Japan, the appointment and briefing of the Deconcentration Review Board, and international reactions, including Soviet protests and Philippine press criticism of proposed rehabilitation programs.

subfiles.about: Chronological summary of FEC papers FEC-292 through FEC-298/2 concerning Japanese economic rehabilitation and Soviet protests.
subfiles.summary: Lists Far Eastern Commission papers concerning U.S. statements on Japanese economic rehabilitation and Soviet inquiries regarding industrial credits.
subfiles.title: Chronological List of Far Eastern Commission Papers Relating to United States Proposals for Economic Rehabilitation in Japan and Soviet Reaction Thereto

subfiles.about: Transmittal of a revised draft reply to the Soviet statement on Japanese industrial credits for Army concurrence.
subfiles.summary: Requests Army Department concurrence on a slightly revised draft statement by General McCoy responding to Soviet FEC inquiries.
subfiles.title: U.S. Reply to Soviet Statement FEC 298/2

subfiles.about: Transmittal of a proposed statement to General McCoy replying to Soviet criticisms of Japanese industrial rehabilitation.
subfiles.summary: Transmits a proposed statement for General McCoy to deliver at the Far Eastern Commission answering the Soviet representative.
subfiles.title: Memorandum for the United States Member, Far Eastern Commission: Proposed Reply to Soviet Statement FEC 298/2
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: Rebuts Soviet claims of illegality regarding U.S. aid for Japanese industrial rehabilitation.
subfiles.summary: Affirms that Potsdam Declaration and FEC policies authorize SCAP to assist Japanese peaceful industries to achieve economic self-support.
subfiles.title: Draft Statement by United States Member, Far Eastern Commission, in Reply to Soviet Statement FEC 298/2

subfiles.about: Proposes strengthening SCAP's Diplomatic Section to guide and coordinate economic policy in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Encloses letter regarding Foreign Service examinations and suggests utilizing SCAP's Diplomatic Section to control war potential and guide policy.
subfiles.title: Letter from William N. Rogers to Robert A. Lovett Concerning SCAP Diplomatic Section

subfiles.about: Warns of economic strains and political risks caused by over 19,000 American military dependents residing in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Reports that housing, services, and extraterritorial privileges for American dependents burden the Japanese economy and urges curtailing arrivals.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Airgram A-75: Number of American Dependents in Japan

subfiles.about: Discusses legislative strategy and encloses draft bills for economic rehabilitation of occupied areas.
subfiles.summary: Transmits agreed drafts of general occupied areas legislation and an alternate bill requesting $220,000,000 for Japan, Korea, and the Ryukyus.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of the Army Kenneth C. Royall to Robert A. Lovett Concerning Occupied Areas Legislation

subfiles.about: Authorizes the President to provide government, relief, economic rehabilitation, reorientation, and reeducation in occupied foreign territories.
subfiles.summary: This proposed legislation authorizes the President to administer occupied foreign territories, maintain public order, and promote economic rehabilitation and reorientation. It provides statutory authority for funding programs to make occupied areas self-supporting and resist totalitarianism, capping Japanese, Korean, and Ryukyuan economic assistance at $220,000,000 for twelve months with Reconstruction Finance Corporation advances. The act also coordinates rehabilitation funding with the Economic Cooperation Act of 1948.
subfiles.title: Draft Bill: Occupied Areas Act of 1948

subfiles.about: Alternative legislation specifically providing $220,000,000 for economic rehabilitation and reorientation in Japan, Korea, and the Ryukyu Islands.
subfiles.summary: Authorizes an appropriation of $220,000,000 and RFC advances up to $40,000,000 for rehabilitation in Japan, Korea, and the Ryukyus.
subfiles.title: Draft Bill: Economic Rehabilitation, Reorientation, and Reeducation in Japan, Korea, and the Ryukyu Islands

subfiles.about: Transmits SCAP Antitrust and Cartels Division papers on the urgency of completing the deconcentration program.
subfiles.summary: Transmits papers prepared by SCAP's Antitrust and Cartels Division supporting the urgent completion of Japan's economic deconcentration program.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 243: Economic Deconcentration Program in Japan

subfiles.about: Comprehensive analysis of Zaibatsu monopoly structures, actions taken under Deconcentration Law No. 207, and guiding administrative principles.
subfiles.from: Antitrust and Cartels Division, ESS, SCAP
subfiles.summary: This report reviews the prewar feudalistic control of the Japanese economy by Zaibatsu holding company combines and domestic cartels, arguing that their dissolution is essential for democratic capitalism. It details measures undertaken by the Holding Company Liquidation Commission, including designating 325 excessive industrial and distributive concentrations and dissolving trading monopolies. It emphasizes that administrative procedures safeguard large-scale productive efficiency and integrated operations while eliminating ownership combines built purely for control.
subfiles.title: Deconcentration Program (Enclosure No. 1 to Despatch No. 243)
subfiles.to: Office of the U.S. Political Advisor for Japan

subfiles.about: Presents twelve recommendations for implementing deconcentration without impairing productive efficiency or economic recovery.
subfiles.from: Antitrust and Cartels Division, ESS, SCAP
subfiles.summary: Presents twelve policy recommendations for eliminating Zaibatsu control, dissolving cartels, dispersing ownership, protecting foreign investors, and speeding economic recovery.
subfiles.title: Recommendations Regarding Economic Deconcentration Program (Enclosure No. 2 to Despatch No. 243)
subfiles.to: Office of the U.S. Political Advisor for Japan

subfiles.about: Describes the background of HCLC commissioners and basic operating principles for the Japanese deconcentration program.
subfiles.summary: Outlines the professional backgrounds of Holding Company Liquidation Commission members and principles ensuring deconcentration supports industrial recovery without rigid formulas.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Economic Deconcentrations (Enclosure No. 3 to Despatch No. 243)

subfiles.about: Submits personnel forms and requests an official State Department letter to facilitate leave from his college.

subfiles.title: Letter from Jerome B. Cohen to Jack E. Lydman Regarding Consultant Appointment

subfiles.summary: Confirms that personnel action was initiated recommending Cohen's appointment as consultant on Japanese and Korean economic research.
subfiles.title: Letter from Jack E. Lydman to Jerome B. Cohen Concerning Consultant Appointment

subfiles.about: Critiques the Office of Economic Affairs' draft briefing outline for the Deconcentration Review Board.
subfiles.summary: Criticizes OE's briefing outline as unbalanced and warns against excessive deconcentration, rapid bank reorganizations, and emergence of black-market wealth.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Proposed Outline for State Department Briefing of Deconcentration Review Board Members

subfiles.about: Draft outline summarizing prewar economic concentrations, policy directives, and remaining deconcentration tasks.
subfiles.summary: Presents briefing outline covering prewar economic combines, U.S. policy evolution, divestiture of Zaibatsu securities, and reorganization of enterprises and banks.
subfiles.title: Proposed Outline for State Department Briefing of Deconcentration Review Board Members

subfiles.about: Biographical roster of the five members appointed to SCAP's Deconcentration Review Board.
subfiles.summary: Lists names and professional backgrounds of the five appointed members of the Deconcentration Review Board.
subfiles.title: Members of Deconcentration Review Board

subfiles.about: Encloses a memorandum on Japanese stabilization and outlines four simultaneous economic reform steps.
subfiles.summary: Transmits an economic memorandum on Japan and recommends simultaneous action on exchange rates, budgets, deconcentration, and wages.
subfiles.title: Letter from William H. Draper, Jr. to Charles E. Saltzman Concerning Japanese Economic Policy

subfiles.about: Concurs with the proposed FEC statement subject to its relation to broad U.S. policy on Japan.
subfiles.summary: Provides Army concurrence for General McCoy's FEC statement subject to its alignment with overall U.S. policy on Japan.
subfiles.title: War Department Memo Routing Slip Concerning U.S. Reply to Soviet Statement FEC 298/2

subfiles.about: Detailed firsthand appraisal of Japanese political developments, economic stabilization, budget balancing, deconcentration, and SCAP administration.
subfiles.summary: This memorandum assesses the critical situation in postwar Japan, highlighting political instability under the new cabinet, aggressive labor wage demands, and stagnant industrial production. It cautions that SCAP's rigid budget-balancing directives could induce severe distress unless accompanied by a realistic exchange rate, private capital revival, and currency stabilization. It also argues that uncertainty over excessive deconcentration paralyzes business initiative and strongly urges trimming SCAP's operational bureaucracy into a compact supervisory body while transferring responsibility to the Japanese.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on the Situation and Economic Problems in Japan

subfiles.about: Transmits Philippine press editorial criticizing American economic aid and reparations reductions for Japan under the Johnston and Draper reports.
subfiles.summary: Transmits a Manila newspaper editorial criticizing U.S. proposals to rehabilitate Japanese industry and reduce reparations at the expense of devastated Asian neighbors.
subfiles.title: Manila Airgram A-225: Philippine Reaction to Johnston and Draper Reports on Japan
